_doc: Canonical organizations registry (t/1217, t/1224). Organizations engaged in AI policy, safety, or development. Cross-POV entities — each carries a pov_alignment map with per-camp score (-1..1) and rationale. topic_engagement links to situations (sit-*); policy_engagement links to policy_actions (pol-*).

organizations.name: Anthropic
organizations.description: AI safety and research company developing large language models with Constitutional AI and Responsible Scaling Policy commitments. Frontier lab that spans acc and saf camps.

accelerationist.rationale: Builds and deploys frontier models rapidly; central voice for scaling laws and capability progress.

safetyist.rationale: Explicit safety-first mission, Responsible Scaling Policy, interpretability research, RSP evals as deployment gate.

skeptic.rationale: Mildly skeptical framing seen as insufficient given deployment pace.

topic_engagement.description: Constitutional AI and RLHF as alignment scaffolding.

key_figures.name: Dario Amodei
key_figures.relevance: Leading voice on responsible scaling and evals-as-gates policy.

organizations.name: OpenAI
organizations.description: Frontier AI lab that trained GPT series and shifted from nonprofit research to capped-profit deployment. Central actor in scaling and commercial deployment; safety framing contested internally.

accelerationist.rationale: Rapid deployment cadence, Sora/GPT-4o launches, embedded strategic bet on capability scaling.

safetyist.rationale: Publishes preparedness framework; safety team departures and dissolution of superalignment team raised concerns.

skeptic.rationale: Nonprofit-to-capped-profit pivot, board turmoil cited as governance drift.

key_figures.name: Sam Altman
key_figures.relevance: Public face of frontier deployment strategy.

organizations.name: Google DeepMind
organizations.description: Google's consolidated AI research organization; Gemini family, AlphaFold, and long-running RL research.

accelerationist.rationale: Backed by Google's compute and deploys frontier models across Google products.

safetyist.rationale: Frontier Safety Framework, dangerous-capability evals, AGI-safety-and-alignment team.

skeptic.rationale: Mixed signals: safety commitments alongside commercial pressure.

organizations.name: xAI
organizations.description: Elon Musk's frontier AI company, developer of Grok. Positions itself as a maximally-truth-seeking alternative to competitor labs.

accelerationist.rationale: Rapid scaling of Colossus cluster and Grok releases with minimal deployment friction.

safetyist.rationale: Publicly critical of what it labels 'woke' safety guardrails; limited published safety evals.

skeptic.rationale: Concentrated ownership and executive-driven direction limit external accountability.

organizations.name: Andreessen Horowitz
organizations.description: Venture capital firm whose partners are among the most vocal accelerationist voices in tech policy discourse.

accelerationist.rationale: Marc Andreessen's 'Techno-Optimist Manifesto' explicitly rejects safety-first framing; firm invests heavily in open-model startups.

safetyist.rationale: Actively campaigns against SB1047 and comparable regulatory proposals.

skeptic.rationale: Skepticism framed as regulatory-capture concern, not distrust of AI capabilities themselves.

topic_engagement.description: Argues open-model dissemination beats gatekept safety.

key_figures.name: Ben Horowitz
key_figures.relevance: Public opposition to prescriptive AI regulation.

organizations.name: Y Combinator
organizations.description: Startup accelerator that funds AI-native companies and generally supports permissive deployment policy.

accelerationist.rationale: Startup-first framing; supports founder-friendly regulatory postures.

safetyist.rationale: Skeptical of frontier-model licensing regimes that would raise startup barriers.

skeptic.rationale: Neutral on distributive concerns.

organizations.name: Center for AI Safety
organizations.description: Nonprofit dedicated to reducing societal-scale AI risks, best known for coordinating the 2023 Statement on AI Risk.

accelerationist.rationale: Frames rapid deployment as increasing existential risk.

safetyist.rationale: Explicit mission is societal-scale AI safety.

skeptic.rationale: Concordant with skeptic worry about harm but different frame (extinction vs distributive).

topic_engagement.description: Coordinated the 2023 Statement on AI Risk.

organizations.name: Future of Life Institute
organizations.description: Nonprofit focused on existential risks including AI. Coordinated the 2023 open letter calling for a six-month pause on frontier training runs.

accelerationist.rationale: Pause letter explicitly targets accelerationist deployment cadence.

safetyist.rationale: Long-standing safety-first mission with concrete campaign coordination.

skeptic.rationale: Aligned on harm concern but framed as extinction rather than distributive.

topic_engagement.description: Pause letter, EU AI Act advocacy.

key_figures.name: Max Tegmark
key_figures.relevance: Public voice on x-risk and pause proposals.

organizations.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute
organizations.description: Pioneering AI alignment research organization; has argued that current alignment approaches are inadequate for superintelligent systems and shifted focus toward advocacy.

accelerationist.rationale: Explicit stance that current deployment cadence is dangerous.

safetyist.rationale: Foundational alignment research with pessimism about tractability.

skeptic.rationale: X-risk frame diverges from skeptic's harm frame.

topic_engagement.description: Publishes on alignment difficulty and now advocates for training halts.

key_figures.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
key_figures.relevance: TIME essay calling to halt frontier training.

organizations.name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
organizations.description: Digital-rights nonprofit that has been actively vocal on AI, privacy, algorithmic accountability, and government surveillance.

accelerationist.rationale: Skeptical of deployment where privacy or civil liberties are at stake.

safetyist.rationale: Aligned on concrete-harm mitigation, not x-risk.

skeptic.rationale: Central voice on surveillance, algorithmic harm, and generative-AI copyright concerns.

organizations.name: AI Now Institute
organizations.description: Research institute focused on the social implications of AI, particularly concentrated power, labor impacts, and civil-rights harms.

accelerationist.rationale: Argues rapid deployment concentrates corporate power.

safetyist.rationale: Critical of x-risk framing as distraction from present harm.

skeptic.rationale: Foundational voice for algorithmic-accountability critique.

organizations.name: Access Now
organizations.description: Global digital-rights nonprofit that advocates for user privacy, freedom of expression, and AI accountability, particularly in vulnerable-population contexts.

accelerationist.rationale: Opposes deployment without accountability mechanisms.

safetyist.rationale: Peripheral overlap on harm-avoidance principles.

skeptic.rationale: Central voice on human-rights-based AI critique.

organizations.name: Mozilla Foundation
organizations.description: Nonprofit organization backing an open, trustworthy internet. Publishes AI transparency research and funds open-model alternatives.

accelerationist.rationale: Supports open-model deployment but with accountability caveats.

safetyist.rationale: Neither central to x-risk nor prescriptive-safety camps.

skeptic.rationale: Public research on trustworthiness gaps, dataset provenance, algorithmic transparency.

organizations.name: NIST
organizations.description: US National Institute of Standards and Technology; hosts the US AI Safety Institute and produces the AI Risk Management Framework.

accelerationist.rationale: Standards-first posture is friction from acc perspective.

safetyist.rationale: AI RMF and USAISI evals seen as safety infrastructure.

skeptic.rationale: Standards work is trust-building, but limited enforcement teeth.

topic_engagement.description: AI RMF v1.0 and generative-AI profile.

organizations.name: European AI Office
organizations.description: European Commission body that oversees implementation and enforcement of the EU AI Act, including the general-purpose AI code of practice.

accelerationist.rationale: AI Act's tiered obligations viewed as deployment friction.

safetyist.rationale: First large-scale enforceable framework for frontier models.

skeptic.rationale: Regulatory venue with meaningful enforcement, though harm coverage debated.

organizations.name: UK AI Safety Institute
organizations.description: UK government-funded institute performing pre-deployment evaluations on frontier models, with voluntary access agreements from major labs.

accelerationist.rationale: Evaluations are lightweight but do add pre-deployment steps.

safetyist.rationale: Concrete third-party evals infrastructure for dangerous-capability testing.

skeptic.rationale: Real teeth on frontier models but constrained scope.

organizations.name: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy
organizations.description: US executive-branch office that shepherded the AI Bill of Rights blueprint and EO 14110 development.

accelerationist.rationale: Frameworks add compliance overhead.

safetyist.rationale: EO 14110 mandated safety testing at scale.

skeptic.rationale: AI Bill of Rights framed around civil-liberties harms.

organizations.name: OECD AI Policy Observatory
organizations.description: Multilateral policy body coordinating the OECD AI Principles adopted by 46+ countries.

accelerationist.rationale: Principles-based framework is low friction.

safetyist.rationale: Multilateral safety norms coordination.

skeptic.rationale: Rights-based framing but soft-law only.

organizations.name: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42
organizations.description: International standards subcommittee producing ISO/IEC AI standards including 42001 (AI Management System) and 23894 (AI Risk Management).

accelerationist.rationale: Standards compliance is manageable but nonzero overhead.

safetyist.rationale: 42001 gives orgs a certifiable safety-management scaffold.

skeptic.rationale: Standards enable auditability, tempered by voluntary adoption.

organizations.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
organizations.description: Interdisciplinary institute producing the annual AI Index Report and cross-disciplinary AI policy research.

accelerationist.rationale: AI Index tracks capability growth with a neutral analytic stance.

safetyist.rationale: Publishes safety and evaluations research.

skeptic.rationale: Covers labor, bias, and concentration-of-power impacts.

organizations.name: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
organizations.description: Long-standing computer-science and AI research laboratory producing foundational research in ML, robotics, and formal methods.

accelerationist.rationale: Basic-research posture; capability contributions widely deployed.

safetyist.rationale: Formal-methods and verification research pertinent to safety.

skeptic.rationale: Neutral academic stance.

organizations.name: Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology
organizations.description: Policy research center focused on the security implications of AI and emerging technologies, particularly compute-governance and export controls.

accelerationist.rationale: Advocates compute-governance policies that would constrain scaling.

safetyist.rationale: National-security frame overlaps with safety-first governance.

skeptic.rationale: Concrete-harm framing (national security), not distributive.

key_figures.name: Helen Toner
key_figures.relevance: Public voice on compute governance and OpenAI board.

organizations.name: RAND Corporation
organizations.description: Longstanding nonprofit policy research organization with growing AI-security and governance program.

accelerationist.rationale: Research often frames deployment risks in security terms.

safetyist.rationale: AI-security research overlaps safetyist policy priorities.

skeptic.rationale: Concrete-harm, security-oriented framing.

organizations.name: Partnership on AI
organizations.description: Multi-stakeholder nonprofit convening tech companies, civil society, and academia on responsible AI practices.

accelerationist.rationale: Voluntary best-practices framework with limited friction.

safetyist.rationale: Coordinates responsible-deployment norms across labs.

skeptic.rationale: Multi-stakeholder inclusion of civil society perspectives.

organizations.name: Meta AI
organizations.description: Meta's foundational AI research group, publisher of the open-weight Llama model family.

accelerationist.rationale: Open-weights release strategy accelerates ecosystem deployment.

safetyist.rationale: Open-weights approach viewed as high-risk under x-risk framing.

skeptic.rationale: Open weights are a mixed signal — democratizes access AND concentrates upstream control.

key_figures.name: Yann LeCun
key_figures.relevance: Public opposition to x-risk framing and pause proposals.
